To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we designed an adaptive control algorithm that can automatically adjust hormone delivery based on glucose measurements and meal announcements by the subject, and we tested this algorithm using a dual-hormone artificial pancreas during an inpatient study in which we used both Dexcom SEVEN and Dexcom G4 PLTINUM continuous glucose monitors.
the system was able not only to maintain glucose levels within a near-normal range but also to eliminate hypoglycemia, which has not been previously demonstrated.

we have successfully designed and clinically evaluated an automated, bihormonal, closed-loop system for the control of blood glucose that uses a fading memory proportional-derivative controller and an adaptive system to estimate the changing sensitivity to insulin.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and implementation of an automated control system for the treatment of diabetes.
the design of an adaptive bihormonal dual-sensor artificial pancreas system that has been evaluated in inpatient studies and shown to improve glycemic control.
the design of a system for automated glycemic control using an adaptive control algorithm and a dual-sensor, dual-hormone approach.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the automated system was able to provide improved glycemic control in comparison with the prestudy condition and the control algorithm was able to adapt the control parameters to changing insulin sensitivity.
the system was able not only to keep subjects' glucose levels in the near-eugylicemic range but also to eliminate hypoglycemia.
the adaptive bihormonal, dual-sensor artificial pancreas is able to maintain glucose levels within the eugylycemic range with no hypoglycemia for the majority of the study time.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
an adaptive, dual-hormone, bihormonal, automated system that uses subcutaneous sensors for both glucose and glucagon and subcutaneous insulin pumps can be designed and used in inpatient studies.
an adaptive control algorithm can be successfully integrated with off-the-shelve sensors and pumps, and can be used to automate the delivery rates of both insulin and glucagon.
the system was able, for the first time, to maintain glucose levels within the eugylycemic range during inpatient studies, with no episodes of severe hypoglycemia.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a bihormonal artificial pancreas that uses subcutaneous glucose and glucagon sensors and pumps is able to maintain glucose levels near normal for extended periods of time.
an adaptive, dual-sensor, bihormonal artificial pancreas system can be designed that can be used to maintain euglycemia and prevent hypoglycemia in patients with type 1 diabetes.
an automated control algorithm can be integrated with off-the-shelve devices to achieve near-euglycaemia.
